title: The Cognitive-Emotional Design and Study of Architectural Space: A Scoping Review of Neuroarchitecture and Its Precursor Approaches
review_question: To present a scoping review of neuroarchitecture and its precursor approaches, mapping out the broad areas on which the new discipline is based, including its limitations, controversies, benefits, impact on professional sectors, and potential.
inclusion_exclusion_criteria: Studies in English, Spanish, German, and Italian; peer-reviewed journals, conference papers, and reference books; human-based studies. Excluded duplicates, wrong topics, content not appropriate for objectives (e.g., bachelor's/master's projects), and non-original data. No date filtering applied.

paper_metadata.crossref_title: The Cognitive-Emotional Design and Study of Architectural Space: A Scoping Review of Neuroarchitecture and Its Precursor Approaches
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: Humans respond cognitively and emotionally to the built environment. The modern possibility of recording the neural activity of subjects during exposure to environmental situations, using neuroscientific techniques and virtual reality, provides a promising framework for future design and studies of the built environment. The discipline derived is termed “neuroarchitecture”. Given neuroarchitecture’s transdisciplinary nature, it progresses needs to be reviewed in a contextualised way, together with its precursor approaches. The present article presents a scoping review, which maps out the broad areas on which the new discipline is based. The limitations, controversies, benefits, impact on the professional sectors involved, and potential of neuroarchitecture and its precursors’ approaches are critically addressed.
